about.base: How results come in, how picks are generated, and what each part does.
Opens the website, picks a state and game, and asks for numbers. The browser only ever talks to the website.

add.engineer: `localhost:4200`; the Screen API, the Analysis engine and the Results store are never reached from the browser.

about.base: The four parts of the suite, started together and wired to each other.

add.engineer: `compose.yaml` in `lotto-options-core` builds the four services from source (`deploy/backend/Dockerfile` for the three JVM services, `deploy/web-ui/Dockerfile` for the website) as the `lotto-stack` project: `results-service`, `core`, `bff` and `web-ui`, each published on `127.0.0.1` and started in that order as each one's health check passes. The Results store reports healthy only once its catalog lists a game, so a first start needs the internet. The Results store and website sources come from sibling clones.

about.base: The screens the user sees: the dashboard, the Smart Generator with its betslip printout, and range analysis (how often winning numbers fall in each band of numbers). Every request goes to the Screen API.

add.engineer: An Angular 21 single-page app, zoneless and standalone. It calls only relative `/ui/*` URLs. nginx serves the built app on port 80 (published as 4200) and proxies `/ui/*` to `${BFF_URL}` with buffering off and a 300 s read timeout; in development `ng serve` with `proxy.conf.json` does the same.

about.base: Takes what the Analysis engine returns and shapes it into exactly what one screen needs. Some dashboard statistics are still worked out here, and are due to move into the engine.

add.engineer: Spring WebFlux on `127.0.0.1:8080`, the only security edge (ADR-0002), serving one view model per screen (ADR-0001, ADR-0003). Endpoints under `/ui`: `ping`, `catalog/states`, `dashboard/{state}/{game}` (plus `/matrix`, `/position-trend`, `/pattern-edge`), `POST dashboard/{state}/{game}/generate`, `POST dashboard/{state}/{game}/betslip/pdf`, `POST range-analysis`. `CoreApiClient` calls five engine endpoints on `core-api.base-url` (`http://localhost:8002`). OpenAPI at `/v3/api-docs`, from which the website generates its types. ADR-0009 records that the assemblers (`FrequencyRollup`, `PositionTrend`, `PatternEdge` and others) still compute statistics that belong in the engine.

set.exec: Turns past draws into suggested picks

about.base: The brains of the suite: game dashboards, suggested numbers, range analysis and printable betslips. Only the Screen API talks to it.

set.exec: Where the value is: it analyses past winning numbers and suggests numbers to play.

add.engineer: Spring Boot on port 8002, one jar (`lotto-options-core-service.jar`) built from the modules in the Engineering view. Health at `/api/v1/gameout/health`. Every module but `core-model` also depends on the Results store's `lottery-result-persistence-service-models` for `LotteryGame`, so `deploy/backend/Dockerfile` builds that first.

tagline.base: Answers requests and does the work

about.base: The part of the engine that runs: it takes requests, works out dashboards and picks, and looks up draw history.

add.engineer: Inbound REST controllers, the application services and the outbound client to the Results store.

tagline.base: Receives requests from the Screen API

about.base: Accepts each request and hands it to the right service.

add.engineer: `AnalysisController` (`/api/v1/analysis`: `GET /{state}/{game}/dashboard`, `POST /generate/numbers`, `POST /range-analysis`), `CatalogController` (`GET /api/v1/catalog/states`), `GameOutController` (`/api/v1/gameout/*`) and `BetslipController` (`POST /api/v1/betslip/pdf`).

about.base: Builds the dashboard's statistics, the range analysis and the printable betslips from a game's past draws.

add.engineer: `LotteryDashboardService` (with the `core-result-analyzer` dashboard analyzers), `LotteryRangeAnalysisService` and `BetslipGenerationService` (PDFBox, with the Texas slip templates under `betslip/Texas/`). The `GameOut*Service`s behind `/api/v1/gameout/*` live here too.

about.base: Gets the game's draw history, then keeps making sets of numbers with the strategy the user chose and checking how each would have done in past draws, for up to about 20 seconds, until it finds a set whose target prize is due.

add.engineer: `LotteryNumberGenerationService.getRandomNumberGeneratedData`. It loads history through `LotteryStateService`, picks a generator from `RandomNumberGeneratorFactory` by the request's `numberGenerator`, and back-tests each set until the `targetedPrizeLevel` has gone unwon for about as many draws as its odds predict, within `SearchLimits.DEFAULT` (25 million comparisons or 20 s). It returns `GeneratedNumberData` with prize-level results.

tagline.base: Fetches past draws from the Results store

about.base: How the engine gets draw data: it asks the Results store for a game's history and waits for the answer.

add.engineer: `WebClientLotteryStateService`, built from `persistence-service.host` (`http://localhost:8001/`) and `persistence-service.games` (`api/v1/state/games`). It blocks on the call on a `boundedElastic` thread. The catalog comes from `GET api/v1/all/v2/state-games`.

about.base: The three ways to pick numbers: Balanced Spread (copies the most common mix of low and high, odd and even numbers in past draws), Secure Random and Fast Random. Also the dashboard analyzers and the ticket scorer.

add.engineer: `LowOddLowEvenHighOddHighEvenLotteryNumberGenerator` and `TemplateMatrixLotteryNumberGenerator` (categorical), `UniformLotteryNumberGenerator` (`SecureRandom`, `ThreadLocalRandom`), the `analyzer.dashboard` analyzers, and `LotteryResultsComparator`.

tagline.base: The shapes of requests and results

about.base: The definitions of what a request and a result look like, shared by the engine and the Screen API so both sides agree.

add.engineer: Such as `RandomNumberGeneratorRequest` and `GeneratedNumberData`. Plain types with Jackson annotations and Lombok; an ArchUnit rule keeps the Results store's types out of it.

tagline.base: Kept for the old desktop app

about.base: Code kept only until the old desktop app is retired. Nothing else in the suite uses it, but it still reads draws from the Results store on its own.

add.engineer: `TicketGenerationController` (`/api/v2/generate-tickets` with its SSE status) and `LottoOptionsCoreController` (`/api/v1/lotto-options-core/games/*`). Packaged in the engine's jar at runtime scope only, so no engine class compiles against it. Deleted with the desktop client.

about.base: Downloads winning numbers, keeps each game's past draws, and answers the engine's questions about them.

set.exec: Keeps every game's winning numbers on file and refreshes itself every two hours.

add.engineer: Spring Boot on port 8001. Modules `lottery-result-persistence-server` (the API), `lottery-result-aggregator` (updating, reading, saving) and `lottery-result-persistence-service-models` (the draw types). No database: the draws are files.

about.base: Lists the states and games on file and returns a game's draw history on request, remembering recent answers until the next refresh.

add.engineer: `PersistenceServiceController` under `/api/v1`: `GET /states`, `GET /states/{stateName}/games`, `GET /all/state-games`, `GET /all/v2/state-games` (the catalog the engine reads), `GET /state-games/{state}` and `POST /state/games` (`{stateName, gameName}` in, a `StateGamesResponse` holding the `LotteryGame` out). Answers come from six in-memory caches (`gameData`, `catalogV1`, `catalogV2`, `stateGameNames`, `states`, `stateGames`); `LotteryDataService` reads a `.ser` file only on a miss.

about.base: Every two hours, and once at start-up, has every game's results refreshed: four games at a time, at most four downloads a second, retrying a game up to three times. A game that fails keeps its previous file.

add.engineer: `DrawResultJob` on cron `0 0 */2 * * ?`, and a `CommandLineRunner` at start-up. `LotteryResultPollingService` runs one task per game on a 4-thread pool, each wrapped in resilience4j retry (3 attempts) and a rate limit of 4 a second, then publishes `PollCompletedEvent` with the counts of games that succeeded, had rows rejected, or failed, even when every game failed.

tagline.base: Downloads and saves each game's results

about.base: Downloads a game's results file, turns its rows into draws, and saves the latest 8,000 of them.

add.engineer: `TexasLotteryHistoryProcessor.processGame` downloads each game's CSV export with `CsvFileReader`, keeps the last `MAX_DRAWS` (8000) rows, parses them into a `LotteryGame` and writes it with `LotteryGameSerializer`. The 17 Texas games are listed under `urls.states` in `application.yml`. A Louisiana PDF reader exists, but its URLs are commented out there.

about.base: Where the draws live: one file per game, replaced whole each time new results come in, so a half-written file is never read.

add.engineer: `LotteryGameSerializer` writes one Java-serialized `LotteryGame` at `{lottery.storage.base-dir}/{STATE}/{Game}.ser` (temp file, fsync, then rename). `base-dir` is `tmp` locally and `/data` in the container, the `draw-data` volume.

about.base: The official source of results. The suite downloads one file per game from it.

add.engineer: Per-game CSV exports under `texaslottery.com/export/sites/lottery/Games/.../Winning_Numbers/`. The only live external source.

about.base:
The suite in one line: the user uses the **website**, the website asks the **Screen API**, the Screen API asks the **Analysis engine**, and the engine gets its draw history from the **Results store**, which keeps itself current from the **Texas Lottery website**.

Click any part for what it does; the other views go one level deeper.

The same suite one level down: what each part contains and which parts talk to each other.

Requests flow from the top down. Draw data flows the other way: the **Results reader** downloads it and the **Draw history service** hands it to the engine.
The Maven modules of **lotto-options-core** by dependency. The Screen API shares only the data formats with the engine.

add.engineer: ADR-0009's target modules (`core-domain`, `core-application`, `core-api-contract`) do not exist yet. The groundwork is done: the legacy quarantine (S19), ArchUnit rules with a frozen, shrink-only baseline (S21, ADR-0010), PMD (S22) and dependency analysis (S23). The module split itself has not started.

about.base: The chosen strategy picks the numbers, and each set is checked against past draws to show what it would have won. This repeats, for up to about 20 seconds, until a set's target prize is due.

add.engineer: The generator chosen by `numberGenerator` through `RandomNumberGeneratorFactory`; `LotteryResultsComparator` scores each set into prize-level results, within `SearchLimits.DEFAULT`.

add.engineer: `GeneratedNumbersAssembler`, called by `SmartGeneratorService`, maps the data to a `GeneratedNumbersViewModel`.

title.base: A tour of the Lotto suite

about.base: The user opens the **website** in a browser and picks a state and a game.

set.exec: Customers use the **website** to choose a game and get suggested numbers.

about.base: The **Screen API** prepares the data for each screen, mostly by reshaping the engine's answers.
The **Analysis engine** does the thinking: dashboards, generated picks, scoring and betslips.

set.exec: The **engine** is where the value is: it turns past draws into suggested picks.

add.engineer: One Spring Boot jar on port 8002, built from the modules in the Engineering view.

about.base: Inside the engine, **Pick generation** runs the strategy the user chose and checks each set against past draws until it finds one worth playing.

add.engineer: A bounded search: 25 million comparisons or 20 s, whichever comes first.

about.base: The **Results store** keeps each game's past draws and refreshes them from the Texas Lottery website every two hours.

set.exec: The **Results store** keeps our data current on its own, with no one to run it.

about.base: Inside the store, the updater has every game refreshed, the reader downloads and saves each game's results, and the history service answers the engine.
